country.name: Norway
country.tagline: A handful of vines near the 59th parallel.

stats.note: Negligible commercial production; no statistics found.

country.overview: Norway makes almost no wine. A few small vineyards in the south, notably Lerkekåsa near Gvarv in Telemark at about 59 degrees north, grow early-ripening and fungus-resistant varieties such as Solaris on sheltered, sun-facing slopes. The state retail monopoly (Vinmonopolet) and a large import market define Norwegian wine culture; domestic production is a curiosity. Norway is outside the EU and has no wine appellations.

history.title: First vineyards
history.text: Small experimental and commercial vineyards appeared in southern Norway, especially in Telemark around Gvarv, known for its fruit growing.

country.climate_soils: Short, cool summers with long daylight; only the most sheltered southern slopes can ripen grapes.

grapes.name: Solaris
grapes.note: The main grape at the few vineyards.
